LanguageData.RHAH_Ending_IdentityFull_Text:
"I am Suiyin, the second princess of the Ratkin Kingdom.

When I was little, the people around me always made the world outside sound lovely. Once I sneaked out of the palace to play, I saw ratkin thin as skeletons carrying heavy loads, gutters full of filth, and people fighting over a mouthful of food. I ran back to ask my parents about it. They scolded me and confined me to my room.

Later I climbed over that wall again. But standing beside those ratkin, I still did not know what I could do. Even now, I am reluctant to give up life in the palace. When I draw, I still think of its gardens. Then I remember the ratkin outside and feel I ought at least to put up some money and try to get supplies to them.

Just call me Suiyin. I have always had that title, but there are still so many questions I do not dare ask aloud."
LanguageData.RHAH_Ending_IdentityPartial_Text:
"I grew up in the palace. Mostly I drew flowers in the gardens, or thought about how to sneak out and play.

That is why I can spare some money and hire people to carry supplies. It was only after I tried paying for it that I realized how little that money could do.

There are other things about my family I hesitate to write. I want to tell you, but when I think of saying them aloud, I find myself clinging to the life I have always had. This is all I can tell you today."
